nodes.label: Goal Photo Placeholders
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary seeded stock photographs, not pictures of the things the goals name. They exist only so the Goals screen can be judged at real density instead of against empty boxes. Licence must be checked before a Play release; all three are deleted once a goal record can store a user-chosen photo.

nodes.label: Modifier.bleed()
nodes.rationale: The single sanctioned escape from the 20dp gutter, used only when an item is the screen's thesis: a thesis about a column of water cannot be delivered inside a card inset on four sides.

nodes.label: Signature: The Submerged Photograph
nodes.rationale: SubmergedPhoto draws the same two-sine swell over a goal's picture at 62% tint so the image reads through the water instead of being painted out, and the level is the goal's own fraction, so the thing you are saving for goes under as you save.

nodes.label: Signature: The Water Column
nodes.rationale: A vertical scrim holds type contrast at any fill level, so the world's own light falloff does the accessibility work rather than a plate behind the text. over = true inverts the reading and turns the fill to alert, always paired with a sign and a written label.

nodes.label: Launcher Icon Vector Drawables
nodes.rationale: Hand-authored vectors, not sourced or generated: three strata of a falling level over the waterline, the same idea the Home hero draws at full size. Ships as-is.

nodes.label: Five-Step Depth Ladder
nodes.rationale: Shelf/Trench/Deep/Night/Abyss, index 0 nearest the light, is both the ground gradient and the source of every plate bed, so one ordering governs the whole screen. Light scheme runs the same five steps from white down.

nodes.label: The Elevation Is Depth Rule
nodes.rationale: A plate's bed alpha and tint are a function of its depth argument and nothing else. Never a drop shadow, never a hand-picked alpha, never a border to fake a lift; there is not one Modifier.shadow in the UI source.

nodes.label: The Lit Column of Water (north star)
nodes.rationale: The figure and the field are the same fact: safe-to-spend is set over a water surface whose fill height is that figure. Material 3 tonal elevation already treats nearer-the-light as lighter, so the metaphor rides the platform instead of fighting it. There is no backdrop blur anywhere, by decision, because Compose at this version has no backdrop filter and a fake blur would be the dishonest half of the material.
nodes.norm_label: the lit column of water (north star)

nodes.label: The No Eyebrow Rule
nodes.rationale: A section heading carries its own weight: title, optional caption, optional trailing text action. No kicker, no numbering, no all-caps label stacked above a heading.

nodes.label: The Photography Rule
nodes.rationale: Photographs appear in exactly one place, a savings goal, where a picture of the thing being saved for does real work. A picture that is not the user's own content is not content: no stock imagery in empty states, no decorative texture, no illustrated onboarding.

nodes.label: 640dp Breakpoint (bar vs rail)
nodes.rationale: Below 640dp a five-item bottom bar, at or above it a leading navigation rail, never a stretched phone bar. The water ground drifts only on Home and Lock, because a background that animates on every screen is a battery bill, not a design.

nodes.label: The Screen Pays Its Own Status Bar Rule
nodes.rationale: The shell's Scaffold deliberately omits the top inset so the Home hero can run under the status bar; each screen re-applies it in exactly one place (TabColumn insetTop, DetailScaffold's app bar insets, the lock screen's windowInsetsPadding). Handing the top inset back to the shell is what put the hero in a box in the first place.
nodes.norm_label: the screen pays its own status bar rule

nodes.label: The Transmission Rule
nodes.rationale: The gradient and its caustics are drawn once behind everything; a plate that paints itself opaque buries the only reason the ground exists.

nodes.label: UI 5.jpg Is Binding
nodes.rationale: The visual world follows one user-supplied reference (deep blue, layered, glassy, hero ring chart, translucent stacked cards); the other four references are taste evidence only. No logo, wordmark, palette or voice guide exists yet and none may be fabricated as pre-existing.

nodes.label: Cost to Build ($0 table)
nodes.rationale: Firebase Spark and Gmail/Drive quotas are quota-capped, not contractually free regardless of usage; thousands of users on one Firebase project could cross into the paid Blaze tier.

nodes.label: Gmail / Drive / Firebase Blocked, Not Deferred
nodes.rationale: Each needs a Google Cloud or Firebase project owned by whoever ships this, with OAuth clients tied to the release signing certificate. There is nothing useful to write until those exist.
nodes.norm_label: gmail / drive / firebase blocked, not deferred

nodes.label: Offline Is The Default State
nodes.rationale: Local-first is the mechanism, not a limitation: the app is fully functional with the network off and sync is an opt-in layer. Offline is a normal state, not an error state.

nodes.label: Bank Aggregation Permanently Excluded
nodes.rationale: Plaid/Yodlee bill per linked account, which breaks the zero-cost constraint at any version; fast manual entry plus free capture paths buy the same completeness.

nodes.label: SMS Auto-Read Permanently Excluded
nodes.rationale: Play policy restricts READ_SMS/RECEIVE_SMS to apps whose core function is SMS handling; a finance app requesting it gets rejected.

nodes.label: Zero Running Cost Forever
nodes.rationale: $0 to build and run except the one-time $25 Play registration. Any feature needing a paid service is cut, not deferred, so the constraint cannot be eroded version by version.

nodes.label: Plaid/Yodlee Aggregation Cut
nodes.rationale: Aggregators charge per linked account with no free tier that suits a shipped consumer app, so it is cut permanently rather than deferred; OCR, email and statement import cover the same catch-every-transaction goal for free.

nodes.label: SMS Auto-Read Not Viable On Play
nodes.rationale: Play restricts READ_SMS/RECEIVE_SMS to default SMS/dialer/Assistant apps; email parsing and statement import are policy-safe and need no sensitive-permission declaration.
nodes.norm_label: sms auto-read not viable on play

nodes.label: Confirmed Stack (Kotlin + Compose M3)
nodes.rationale: Exchange rates use HttpURLConnection and the framework JSON parser because one GET returning one small object does not need an HTTP library.

nodes.label: Totals Derived At Read Time
nodes.rationale: LedgerState computes every headline figure from the ledger on read; an account balance is the opening figure plus every transaction since, never a stored total that can drift from the rows.

nodes.label: No Chart Library (Canvas charts)
nodes.rationale: The design needs a ring with labels on the arc and a mirrored net-worth sounding that neither Vico nor MPAndroidChart draws, and a chart library brings its own house style into a committed visual world.

nodes.label: No Hilt
nodes.rationale: One database, one repository, one view model: MoneyApp is the whole dependency graph in twenty lines. Swapping to Hilt later changes nothing above it.

nodes.label: Not Verified At All
nodes.rationale: Everything that needs a screen, a camera or a network is untested: no UI test has ever run, notification delivery, the biometric prompt and OCR accuracy have never been exercised, and Room migrations are uncovered.

nodes.label: Nothing Derived From Unkept Periods
nodes.rationale: A challenge stops counting at the first transaction on record, so a fresh install is never handed a week of discipline it did not earn.

nodes.label: Gamification Is A Layer Over Real Data
nodes.rationale: Challenges are computed on every read and never stored, so there is no joined flag and no opt-in. The trade is that a user cannot start a challenge deliberately; what they get instead is an app that cannot claim a run their ledger does not support, and nothing to repair when an import or an undo rewrites history underneath it.
nodes.norm_label: gamification is a layer over real data

nodes.label: Hilt Deliberately Absent
nodes.rationale: One database, one repository and one view model do not need a dependency-injection framework; MoneyApp is the whole graph in twenty lines and swapping to Hilt later changes nothing above it.

nodes.label: JDK 15 vs AGP 8.7 Toolchain Gap
nodes.rationale: The system JDK is 15, which AGP 8.7 rejects, so Android Studio's bundled JDK is the expected build environment. No emulator or system image is installed, so nothing has been verified against a rendered screen.

nodes.label: Signature: Hand-drawn Charts
nodes.rationale: Ring labels ride their own arc as real text nodes instead of sitting in a legend, so TalkBack reads the ring as a list. No chart library: a kit brings its own gridlines and categorical rainbow into a committed world, and theming arguments never get them back out.

nodes.label: Merchant Monogram
nodes.rationale: The disc tint is a function of the merchant's own name hashed into categoryScale(), so one merchant keeps one colour forever and a column of rows stops looking like a column of the same row; the category survives as a small badge.

nodes.label: No Date Picker When Logging
nodes.rationale: Everything logs as now to keep the hurry path short; bills and goals do get a picker.

nodes.label: SQL Has A Floor (minSdk 26 SQLite)
nodes.rationale: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE needs SQLite 3.24, which did not arrive until API 30. It was in MerchantMemoryDao.remember, which runs on every manually logged transaction, and it threw on Android 8, 9 and 10. UPDATE-then-INSERT is the portable upsert.

nodes.label: Logging Must Survive A Hurry
nodes.rationale: The add-transaction path is the most optimized path in the app because the core moment is one-handed, in public, before the user forgets; everything else can afford a tap.

nodes.label: RepositoryWriteTest (write paths)

nodes.label: Archivo Variable Type Scale
nodes.rationale: Archivo run wide (wdth 112-118) gives figures a broad engineered stance; the same family at wdth 100 keeps headings in the family without competing with the money. Width is earned: wide means the number is real money.
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused

nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused

nodes.label: Customization (feature area 10)
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused

nodes.label: No Material You by default
nodes.rationale: The depth palette is what makes the waterline legible; a wallpaper-derived scheme reorders it. Offered as an explicit opt-in in Settings > Appearance.
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused

nodes.label: The Cents Are Shown Rule
nodes.rationale: Money is Long minor units formatted by moneyParts; cents are always present and never emphasised (64% size, 52% alpha). Never Double, never rounded away.
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused

nodes.label: Dynamic Color Off By Default
nodes.rationale: A wallpaper-derived scheme reorders the depth ladder until the waterline stops meaning anything, so it is opt-in in Appearance.
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused

nodes.label: No Control Wired To Nothing
nodes.rationale: Either a control acts, or it is disabled with a stated reason, or it is not drawn; a button that absorbs a tap in silence is the one defect a user cannot diagnose. The condition that would refuse a tap belongs in enabled, never in an early return inside onClick.
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused

nodes.label: The Real FAB Rule
nodes.rationale: One floating action per screen, and only where the primary action exists. A FAB that does nothing is worse than no FAB, and a circular add button inside the navigation bar is an iOS tab-bar habit.
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused

nodes.label: The Real Money Rule
nodes.rationale: A figure the eye lands on or scans down a column is rendered through MoneyText in a MoneyType style; money inside a running sentence uses money() in the sentence's style, because tabular figures exist to align a column and there is no column inside a sentence. Counts, percentages and day numbers are not money. The Glance widget is the one exception, and not by choice: it has no access to the app's font.
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused

nodes.label: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused
nodes.rationale: Transfers, goal contributions and debt payments all return whether they happened, because a write that silently does not happen is the worst outcome available: the user believes it did.
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused
nodes.norm_label: a cross-currency write converts or is refused

nodes.label: Nothing Posts Without The User Confirming
nodes.rationale: Capture assists (OCR, email, statement import) always pre-fill for confirmation and never post silently; automation pre-fills, the user commits.
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused
nodes.norm_label: nothing posts without the user confirming

nodes.label: The Number Must Be Right Before It Is Beautiful
nodes.rationale: Money data is never rounded, estimated, or animated into ambiguity; it is the user's own real money and wrong numbers are the worst possible failure.
nodes.community_name: A Cross-Currency Write Converts Or Is Refused
nodes.norm_label: the number must be right before it is beautiful

nodes.label: The One Warm Hue Rule
nodes.rationale: Sun means goals and streaks and nothing else, and is excluded from categoryScale() on purpose, so a warm mark anywhere in the app means exactly one thing.

nodes.label: The Arriving Curve Rule
nodes.rationale: Material's FastOutSlowInEasing belongs to something travelling between two on-screen positions; it accelerates in, and nothing arriving should accelerate in. Reaching for the familiar standard curve already put the wrong easing on every entrance in this app once.

nodes.label: The Expenses Are Not Red Rule
nodes.rationale: In a tracker you log expenses all day; painting each one as an alarm makes the alarm meaningless. Expense amounts take Expense Ink and only over-budget and overdue reach for alert.
nodes.norm_label: the expenses are not red rule

nodes.label: The Feedback Is Not A Gesture Rule
nodes.rationale: Material's own feedback grammar (press state, spring settle on a keypress, haptic at commit) is not a second authored motion and needs no justification against the filling gesture; what it must never do is animate something not responding to a user action in that moment.
nodes.norm_label: the feedback is not a gesture rule

nodes.label: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
nodes.rationale: Every amount has a sign and sits in a tabular column, and every over state pairs its tone with a written label, so a screen reader and a colour-blind eye get the same fact.

nodes.label: The One Authored Motion Rule
nodes.rationale: The app has one authored gesture and it is filling; every other animated surface is a quieter instance of the same gesture, so there is no second hero motion in a different idiom. Every animated surface reads motionEnabled() first and collapses to a zero-duration tween when Remove animations is on.

nodes.label: The Reveal Plays Once Rule
nodes.rationale: A LazyColumn disposes an item when it scrolls out, so a bare animateFloatAsState replays the reveal on every scroll back and the gesture becomes a loop the user triggers by scrolling. rememberFill keeps its played flag in rememberSaveable and comes back already full.

nodes.label: Accessibility and Inclusion Commitments
nodes.rationale: Dynamic type must not clip money values, 48dp minimum targets, colour is never the only carrier of the income/expense distinction, one-handed use stays possible, and both themes ship.

nodes.label: Only Two Permissions
nodes.rationale: POST_NOTIFICATIONS for bill reminders, asked at the toggle and never at startup; INTERNET only for the exchange-rate lookup, whose request carries a currency code and no identifier. No camera permission (system camera app is delegated to) and no storage permission (receipt photos live in app-private storage).

nodes.label: Bills, Goals and Debts Read Currency From Their Account
nodes.rationale: A stored currency column would be a second home for the same fact, free to disagree with the first.
nodes.norm_label: bills, goals and debts read currency from their account

nodes.label: Multi-Currency Conversion Policy
nodes.rationale: Accounts hold their own currency, every total converts into the base, and a currency with no rate is left out of the total and named on screen. Forty euros shown as forty dollars because a rate was missing is not an approximation, it is a wrong figure with a currency symbol on it.

nodes.label: Emergency Fund Savings Goal
nodes.rationale: A seeded or default savings goal in the app. The existence of a matching drawable implies goals carry a cover image keyed by goal identity, alongside target amount and progress.
nodes.community_name: Emergency Fund Goal Cover Photo (City Skyline)

nodes.label: Portrait 4:5 Hero Crop for Goal Cards
nodes.rationale: Tall portrait aspect (roughly 4:5), consistent with a goal card hero or full-bleed goal detail header in a vertically scrolling list, not a wide banner.
nodes.community_name: Emergency Fund Goal Cover Photo (City Skyline)
nodes.norm_label: portrait 4:5 hero crop for goal cards

nodes.label: Emergency Fund Goal Cover Photo (City Skyline)
nodes.rationale: Stock urban skyline photograph (dense Manhattan-style high-rise blocks, hazy pastel sky, high vantage point). Not a UI screenshot, chart or diagram: it is decorative cover art for the built-in 'Emergency Fund' savings goal. The aspirational-but-sober city framing signals stability and security rather than a reward or splurge goal.
nodes.community_name: Emergency Fund Goal Cover Photo (City Skyline)
nodes.norm_label: emergency fund goal cover photo (city skyline)

nodes.label: goal_<name> Cover Art Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: File named goal_emergency.jpg: the goal_<key> prefix lets goal cover art be resolved by identifier (resource-name lookup or a key to drawable map) rather than each goal hardcoding a drawable reference. Adding a goal type means dropping in goal_<key>.jpg.
nodes.community_name: Emergency Fund Goal Cover Photo (City Skyline)

nodes.label: Muted Desaturated Palette for Text Overlay Legibility
nodes.rationale: Low-saturation neutrals (warm brick, grey-blue glass, pale sky) with no high-chroma focal point and a bright, low-detail sky band across the top. This keeps white or scrim-backed text (goal name, amount saved, progress) legible over the image and lets it sit under a Material theme without clashing.
nodes.community_name: Emergency Fund Goal Cover Photo (City Skyline)
nodes.norm_label: muted desaturated palette for text overlay legibility

nodes.label: drawable-nodpi Photographic Asset Bucket
nodes.rationale: Placed in drawable-nodpi so the photo ships once and is never density-scaled by the resource system. Trade-off: one moderate-resolution JPEG instead of an mdpi..xxxhdpi ladder, keeping APK size down at the cost of sharpness on high-density screens. JPEG rather than PNG or vector because it is a photograph.
nodes.community_name: Emergency Fund Goal Cover Photo (City Skyline)
